subject: ThermoFlow discovery: integration eligibility + architecture next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Megan Lopez <megan.lopez@thermoflow.com>, Diego Rivas <diego.rivas@thermoflow.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ThermoFlow discovery: integration eligibility + architecture next steps

Hi Megan / Diego —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the technical deep-dive: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary workloads: chat + long-form summarization for engineering tickets (~1.5k tokens median, spikes to 6–8k).
- Secondary: embeddings for semantic search + a reranker for top-k re-scoring.
- Compliance ask: EU data residency, long-term audit logs, and a SOC2 questionnaire currently in process.

Immediate integration considerations
- SDK/Auth: we support API keys and short-lived JWTs via your IdP (SAML/OIDC). Recommend short-lived tokens for client-side telemetry and server-side service account for backend calls.
- Routing: suggest region-preferring policy (eu-primary, us-failover) + model-cost tiers. Example policy: prefer small-quantized models for embeddings, route high-latency-sensitive calls to dedicated capacity.
- Structured output / tool-calling: we can enable function-calling; we'll add a schema contract for your ticketing actions.
- Embeddings & reranker: use dense embeddings with an FAISS index; reranker runs on hosted GPU pool as a second-pass.

Attachments: I attached a first-draft routing diagram (routing-proposal-v1.png) — it shows region routing, fallback chain, and where KV-caching lives.

Ask / next steps
1) Can you share the filled security questionnaire (SOC2 progress + infra controls)?
2) Confirm expected QPS and peak concurrent requests for chat & rerank (helps sizing Dedicated vs Hosted).
3) Are you planning an on-prem requirement or is VPC with EU hosting enough?

If that looks right, propose a 30-min technical deep-dive next week (we'll include Karthik from solutions and Marissa from product for model-routing discussion).

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: routing-proposal-v1.png (image/png)]
From: Megan Lopez <megan.lopez@thermoflow.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ThermoFlow discovery: integration eligibility + architecture next steps

Thanks Logan — good summary. A few clarifying Qs before the deep-dive: 

- Embeddings: we currently store vectors in-house (self-hosted FAISS). Can Redwood accept a push-only embedding workflow (we push vectors; scoring/rerank can call Redwood endpoints)? Any bandwidth/ingest limits we should plan for?
- Reranker latency: our SLA target is 150ms p99 for re-ranking top-20. Is that achievable with hosted rerankers, or would we need Dedicated?
- Function/tool calling: we're planning one-way actions (create/update ticket) and would like signed webhook callbacks back to our platform. Any recommendations for retry/backoff and idempotency?

I've attached the security questionnaire we have so far — it's incomplete but should help (ThermoFlow_Security_Questionnaire.pdf).

Thanks,
Megan Lopez
Head of Platform Engineering
ThermoFlow

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Megan Lopez <megan.lopez@thermoflow.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 13:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ThermoFlow discovery: integration eligibility + architecture next steps

Megan — thanks, received the questionnaire. Quick answers and an ops proposal before the deep-dive: 

1) Embeddings push-only flow
- Yes. You can continue to host the FAISS index. Recommended pattern: push embeddings to your index and call Redwood for rerank/second-pass by sending only ids + candidate vectors or compressed context. This keeps your vector store sovereign and limits token transfer. We have rate guidance: sustained ingest is fine up to 200 qps for metadata + embeddings; larger sustained rates should be scoped for Dedicated.

2) Reranker latency
- 150ms p99 is aggressive for a hosted multi-tenant reranker on cold starts. Two options:
  a) Hosted with warm-up: we can maintain a warmed GPU pool for your rerankers (cost-effective for moderate volume). Expect ~200–300ms p99 baseline, but we can tune kernel selection and batching to approach 150ms.
  b) Dedicated pool: guaranteed latency SLO (150ms p99) with reserved capacity and KV cache pinned to nodes. This is the recommended path if strict SLO is required.

3) Function/tool calling best practices
- Signed callbacks + HMAC verification, idempotency tokens on your side, exponential backoff from our side with jitter (we support 5 retries with exponential backoff). We'll provide sample header X-Redwood-Sig and replay window guidance.

Proposed low-friction POC plan
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): Hosted API integration + embedding push test; evaluate reranker latency on sample production traffic.
- Phase 2 (2–4 weeks): If p99 > 180ms, migrate reranker onto a short-term Dedicated reservation for baseline SLO.

I've uploaded a concise options doc that compares Hosted vs Dedicated cost/latency tradeoffs (architecture-options-20270426.pdf).

Next step: can we book a 30-min technical deep-dive Wed 28 Apr or Thu 29 Apr? I'll include Karthik to walk through SDK/auth and Marissa for routing policy decisions.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
